name: Zero Trust
mantra: Never trust, always verify every request
when_to_apply: Designing NSG/ASG micro-perimeters for workload traffic
Implementing Entra ID RBAC across application layers
When assuming breach posture for mission-critical workloads
Segmenting PaaS access via Private Link/Endpoints
without_it: Single breach enables lateral movement across flat network topology
Implicit service-to-service trust bypasses RBAC and NSG controls
Overly permissive network policies persist undetected without continuous verification
Insider threats exploit missing micro-segmentation; compliance audits fail
key_tradeoff: More verification granularity means more latency and Entra ID/Firewall Premium complexity

name: Reliability Design Principles
mantra: Design every workload to survive failure gracefully
when_to_apply: Architecting new mission-critical workloads on Azure
Running failure mode analysis across critical flows
Defining RTO/RPO/SLA targets with stakeholders
When trading off redundancy cost against uptime
without_it: Single-zone outage cascades into full workload failure
No RTO/RPO targets means unbounded recovery time
Reliability targets misaligned with actual business impact tiers
Reactive firefighting replaces self-healing and automation
key_tradeoff: More redundancy and active/active regions means higher cost and operational complexity

name: Assume Breach
mantra: Defend every layer as if already compromised
when_to_apply: Designing micro-segmentation and blast radius containment
Planning encryption for data at-rest and in-transit
Building incident response and DR runbooks
Architecting zero-trust access with Entra Conditional Access
without_it: Single NSG misconfiguration yields full lateral movement across VNets
Unencrypted east-west traffic enables silent data exfiltration post-breach
No micro-segmentation means one compromised pod owns entire cluster
Missing Log Analytics audit trails delay breach detection beyond RTO
key_tradeoff: More defense-in-depth layers cost operational complexity and latency

name: Four Vs Of Big Data
mantra: Profile volume, velocity, variety, veracity before selecting services
when_to_apply: Designing mission-critical data platform on Azure
Choosing between Cosmos DB, ADLS, Event Hubs
Defining P50/P99 latency and throughput targets
Assessing data quality gates for pipeline governance
without_it: Cosmos DB partition limits hit causing downtime and data loss
Pipelines throttled under real-time ingestion; Event Hubs backpressure cascades
Schema drift breaks downstream consumers across polyglot datastores
Decisions built on unvalidated data erode reliability SLA compliance
key_tradeoff: Optimizing all four Vs simultaneously multiplies cost and complexity; prioritize per workload SLA

name: Design For Recovery
mantra: Engineer recovery paths before failure strikes
when_to_apply: Defining RTO/RPO targets per business criticality tier
Deploying stateful services requiring zone-redundant replication
Selecting active-passive cold/warm standby DR patterns
Planning failover across availability zones or regions
without_it: RTO breach: no tested restore path extends outage indefinitely
RPO breach: asynchronous gaps cause permanent data loss
Cascading failures propagate through undocumented dependency chains
Ad-hoc recovery attempts trigger split-brain or data corruption
key_tradeoff: More recovery capability (multi-region, warm standby) means higher cost and complexity

name: Least Privilege
mantra: Grant minimum access, scope, and duration
when_to_apply: Assigning RBAC roles to identities or pipelines
Configuring Entra PIM for production control plane
Designing Key Vault or API authorization scopes
Auditing existing permissions for privilege drift
without_it: Compromised managed identity escalates across entire subscription
Standing access enables malicious admin Key Vault secret deletion
Broad RBAC assignment exposes production data plane to breach
Overprivileged accounts fail SE:05 audit and block incident isolation
key_tradeoff: Tighter RBAC and PIM activation reduce blast radius but add latency and Entra ID dependency

name: Zero-Downtime Deployment
mantra: Deploy beside, shift traffic, decommission old.
when_to_apply: Releasing new versions of mission-critical workloads
Applying infrastructure changes to production scale units
Rolling out hotfixes under active user traffic
Migrating backends bound by 99.99%+ SLA targets
without_it: Maintenance windows erode 99.99% composite availability targets
Failed deployments cause full stamp outages without rollback path
Customer-visible 5xx errors during release rollouts breach SLOs
Fear-driven culture produces infrequent high-risk big-bang deploys
key_tradeoff: Transient blue/green infrastructure duplication costs more but eliminates deployment-induced downtime.

name: Design For Resilience
mantra: Bend under failure, never break entirely.
when_to_apply: Architecting across multiple Azure failure domains
Defining SLA/RTO/RPO for critical workload flows
Hardening critical path after Failure Mode Analysis
Planning graceful degradation for dependency outages
without_it: Single component failure cascades into total system outage
No circuit breakers; dependent service failures propagate everywhere
Users hit hard 500 errors instead of degraded functionality
Equal redundancy spend on non-critical and critical paths
key_tradeoff: More resilience patterns and redundancy means more architectural complexity and cost.

name: Verify Explicitly
mantra: Validate every identity, action, location, every time
when_to_apply: Authenticating users or services via Entra ID
Processing data plane requests from any source
Granting access across network or trust boundaries
When requests originate from unexpected locations or devices
without_it: Implicit trust enables lateral movement after single credential compromise
Compromised managed identities persist undetected without continuous validation
Unauthorized data modifications corrupt integrity, violating RPO guarantees
Over-privileged access expands blast radius across subscriptions and tenants
key_tradeoff: Stronger per-request verification adds authentication latency and user friction

name: Cost-Efficiency Mindset
mantra: Spend only what workloads need, maximize ROI
when_to_apply: Designing new workload SKU and scaling choices
Reviewing Azure Cost Management monthly reports
Provisioning dev/test environments with lower SKUs
Evaluating scale-up versus right-sizing existing resources
without_it: Overprovisioned VMs and idle resources inflate monthly burn rate
No chargeback accountability leads to unowned orphaned resources
Dev/test environments running production-tier SKUs waste 40%+ spend
Reactive cost alerts fire after budget overruns already occurred
key_tradeoff: Aggressive cost reduction risks degraded reliability, performance, or delivery velocity

name: Design For Rate Optimization
mantra: Squeeze maximum value from every committed dollar.
when_to_apply: Choosing between Reserved Instances and pay-as-you-go
Negotiating Savings Plans or enterprise agreement renewals
Applying Azure Hybrid Benefit to eligible workloads
When Log Analytics ingest patterns become predictable
without_it: Pay-as-you-go defaults waste 30-60% vs Reserved Instance pricing
Unused Azure Hybrid Benefit entitlements strand license value indefinitely
Log Analytics per-GB tier bleeds cost despite stable daily ingest
Single-tenant deployments miss co-location density savings across teams
key_tradeoff: Deeper commitment discounts cost consumption flexibility and risk underutilization waste.

name: Defense in Depth
mantra: Stack redundant security layers at every boundary
when_to_apply: Designing NSG, Azure Firewall, and WAF segmentation
Implementing compensating controls from threat modeling output
Architecting multi-tier apps handling PII or secrets
Applying Zero Trust across identity, network, data planes
without_it: Single WAF bypass grants full access to backend resources
Lateral movement spreads undetected across flat VNet topologies
One misconfigured NSG rule exposes entire subnet to internet
Compromised identity escalates unchecked without layered authorization gates
key_tradeoff: More security layers means more latency, cost, and operational complexity

name: Blast Radius
mantra: Contain every failure before it spreads.
when_to_apply: Designing fault isolation via stamps or bulkheads
Evaluating multi-tenant noisy-neighbor co-location risks
Planning progressive rollouts across deployment stages
Mapping single-component failure impact on dependent flows
without_it: Single AZ fault cascades across entire workload, breaching SLA
Noisy-neighbor resource exhaustion causes cross-tenant outages
Security compromise spreads unchecked through co-located subscriptions
Incident responders lack impact scope, extending MTTR significantly
key_tradeoff: Smaller blast radius costs more isolation boundaries and operational complexity.

name: Automation
mantra: Automate everything you'd regret doing twice
when_to_apply: Deploying infrastructure or application changes via CI/CD
Scaling workloads through VMSS or autoscale rules
Executing progressive exposure rollouts across environments
Remediating alerts via Azure Functions or runbooks
without_it: Manual deployments cause configuration drift, outages, and extended RTO
Inconsistent environments produce unreproducible bugs across stages
Slow incident response degrades SLA from minutes to hours
Operations bottleneck—teams cannot scale beyond handful of workloads
key_tradeoff: Upfront IaC and pipeline investment costs velocity now; manual processes cost reliability forever

name: Cost-Management Discipline
mantra: Make every dollar visible, owned, intentional.
when_to_apply: Standing up new workloads or landing zones
During monthly/quarterly Cost Management reviews
When Azure Monitor cost alerts fire unexpectedly
Onboarding teams to shared subscription infrastructure
without_it: Untagged resource sprawl triggers bill shock across subscriptions
No owner accountable when Cost Management flags overruns
Optimization stays reactive—no cost model drives proactive rightsizing
Cannot justify SLA penalty budget vs. reliability investment spend
key_tradeoff: Rigorous cost tracking overhead costs team delivery velocity and agility.

name: Design For Usage Optimization
mantra: Eliminate idle capacity, extract maximum resource value
when_to_apply: Costs growing faster than business value delivered
VMSS or App Service instances idle off-peak
When usage patterns justify Reserved Instance commits
Active-passive deployments waste standby capacity
without_it: Overprovisioned VMSS burns budget at 15% CPU utilization
Idle standby regions cost 100% while serving zero traffic
Missed 40-72% savings from Reserved Instance commitments
High spend still breaches SLAs from misallocated resources
key_tradeoff: Higher utilization targets reduce cost headroom for unexpected demand spikes

name: CAP Theorem
mantra: Partition happens—choose consistency or availability now
when_to_apply: Selecting Cosmos DB consistency levels for global distribution
Architecting multi-region active/active deployment patterns
Defining RPO/RTO targets for distributed data stores
Evaluating strong vs eventual consistency per workload
without_it: Cosmos DB strong consistency chosen globally, halving write availability
Eventual consistency surprises cause stale reads in financial workflows
Multi-region failover assumes zero data loss despite async replication
Database selection ignores partition behavior, causing split-brain outages
key_tradeoff: Stronger consistency costs higher latency and reduced availability during partitions

name: Self-Preservation
mantra: Every component protects itself; failures stay local.
when_to_apply: Implementing circuit-breaker, bulkhead, or retry patterns
Designing service boundaries in distributed workloads
Evaluating cascading failure risks across dependencies
Planning graceful degradation during partial outages
without_it: Single App Service failure cascades into full workload outage
Unbounded upstream retries overwhelm downstream services causing retry storms
Localized dependency timeout triggers correlated multi-region SLA breach
No graceful degradation; binary healthy-or-dead system behavior
key_tradeoff: Stronger isolation via bulkheads and circuit breakers costs added latency and complexity.

name: Design For Operations
mantra: Shift left—detect failure before customers do
when_to_apply: Architecting new production workloads on Azure
Defining CI/CD pipelines with blue/green deployments
Establishing Azure Monitor and Application Insights alerting
Preparing incident response runbooks and chaos experiments
without_it: Failures surface via customer complaints, not Azure Monitor alerts
Zero telemetry during outages makes MTTR unbounded
Chaotic incident response without runbooks extends downtime hours
Recurring outages persist—no root cause data captured
key_tradeoff: 20-40% sprint capacity for observability costs feature velocity but slashes MTTR

name: Observable Systems
mantra: Unseen failures become customer-facing outages fast.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed microservices across Azure Monitor stack
Building layered health models for critical workloads
Troubleshooting correlated failures across service dependencies
Onboarding SRE teams with alerting and dashboards
without_it: Blind spots extend MTTR; SLA breaches cascade silently.
Incident response degrades to guesswork without correlated traces.
Transient vs non-transient failures indistinguishable; wrong remediation fires.
No health model means no automated degradation detection.
key_tradeoff: More telemetry depth improves MTTR but increases Monitor ingestion cost and noise.

name: Simplicity
mantra: Shrink surface area before controlling it
when_to_apply: Designing greenfield architectures from requirements
Reviewing systems with recurring misconfigurations
Choosing between zone-redundant and multi-region patterns
Consolidating redundant services or components
without_it: Sprawling ARM/Bicep configs no single engineer fully understands
Misconfigured NSGs or RBAC causing preventable outages
Slower MTTR as responders trace hidden dependency chains
Standards drift as teams build undocumented workarounds
key_tradeoff: More simplicity means less flexibility; zone-redundant beats multi-region unless RTO demands otherwise

name: Segmentation
mantra: Draw boundaries before attackers draw theirs.
when_to_apply: Designing VNet topology with NSGs and ASGs
Isolating sensitive data stores from general compute
Planning multi-tenant or multi-environment architectures
Containing blast radius after breach or incident
without_it: Single breach enables lateral movement across entire environment
Flat network defeats Zero Trust; NSG/ASG policies unenforced
No distinct security policies per workload tier blocks compliance
Blast radius spans all tenants destroying SLA commitments
key_tradeoff: Finer micro-perimeters increase containment but multiply NSG/policy complexity and cost.

name: PACELC Theorem
mantra: No partition? Still trade latency for consistency.
when_to_apply: Choosing Cosmos DB consistency level for multi-region writes
Evaluating session vs strong consistency impact on P99
Designing active/active replication across paired regions
Comparing bounded-staleness vs eventual for read-heavy workloads
without_it: CAP analysis ignores normal-operation latency penalty from strong consistency
Strong consistency adds cross-region round-trips destroying sub-100ms P99 targets
Eventual consistency causes stale reads violating business correctness requirements
Cosmos DB RU costs spike from unnecessary strong consistency overhead
key_tradeoff: Lower read latency costs weaker consistency guarantees even without partitions.

name: Design For Self-Healing
mantra: Automate remediation before humans notice failures
when_to_apply: Transient failures common across distributed components
Manual response too slow for SLA recovery
Known failure modes have automatable remediation paths
Scale exceeds human operator response capacity
without_it: Transient faults cascade into full outages without circuit breakers
Alert fatigue buries ops teams in repetitive manual fixes
MTTR explodes waiting for human diagnosis of automatable failures
SLA breaches from recovery times exceeding RTO targets
key_tradeoff: More upfront remediation logic complexity means less operational toil and faster MTTR

name: Design For Scale-Out
mantra: Add more units, never bigger units.
when_to_apply: When demand spikes exceed single-instance vertical limits
Deploy stateless or partitionable workloads across stamps
Fault tolerance requires redundant parallel instances
Cost optimization demands elastic VMSS/AKS capacity
without_it: Hard throughput ceiling when VM/AKS node limits hit
Single-instance failure causes full workload outage, RTO blown
Over-provisioned SKUs waste spend during low-demand periods
Upgrade-induced downtime scaling vertically to larger SKUs
key_tradeoff: Scale-out elasticity costs state management and data consistency complexity.

name: Mission-Critical Design
mantra: Treat every resource as disposable, nothing irreplaceable.
when_to_apply: Targeting 99.99%+ SLOs with near-zero RTO/RPO
Building workloads where failure cost is catastrophic
Architecting stateless scale-unit stamps on AKS
Planning multi-region active-active with Front Door
without_it: Single points of failure collapse entire workloads during zonal outages
Stateful components create recovery bottlenecks exceeding RPO targets
Regional failure requires manual rebuild instead of automated stamp redeployment
Tightly coupled dependencies trigger cascading failures across scale units
key_tradeoff: Maximum reliability via ephemeral deployment stamps costs higher complexity and spend.

name: Design Principles
mantra: Anchor every decision to principles before patterns.
when_to_apply: Starting new mission-critical workload design
Resolving conflicts across WAF pillars
Reviewing architecture decisions for consistency
Onboarding engineers to design rationale
without_it: Contradictory decisions across pillars degrade reliability and security simultaneously
Over-optimizing reliability tanks performance via replication latency
Unjustifiable architecture choices fail stakeholder and compliance reviews
Design drift emerges as system evolves without principled guardrails
key_tradeoff: Strict principle adherence costs flexibility when novel constraints demand pragmatic exceptions.

name: STRIDE
mantra: Hunt all six threat categories before attackers.
when_to_apply: Threat modeling new or changed architecture components
Reviewing authentication and authorization trust boundaries
Assessing data flow diagrams for security gaps
Preparing for security design reviews
without_it: Entire threat categories unexamined; elevation-of-privilege paths persist silently
Ad-hoc analysis misses repudiation risks lacking Azure Monitor audit trails
Teams fixate on DDoS while spoofing and tampering vectors fester
No structured coverage across Entra ID, WAF, DDoS Protection layers
key_tradeoff: Breadth across six threat categories costs depth in any single vector.

name: Criticality
mantra: Tier every flow before engineering resilience
when_to_apply: Rating user/system flows against criticality scale
Allocating budget across components with different SLAs
Deciding active/active vs active/passive per flow
Triaging incidents under pressure
without_it: Active/active multi-region deployed for low-value flows—budget wasted
Critical paths get single-region; outage cascades to revenue loss
Flat 99.9% SLO masks flows needing 99.999% composite targets
Incident response treats batch jobs equal to payment flows
key_tradeoff: Stricter RTO/RPO per tier costs more regions, replicas, and operational complexity

name: Fault Isolation
mantra: Contain blast radius, protect critical paths always
when_to_apply: Drawing boundaries between different-criticality components
Deploying shared infrastructure serving multiple workloads
Introducing third-party or unreliable dependencies
Running Failure Mode Analysis on distributed flows
without_it: Single zone failure cascades into full multi-region outage
Non-critical dependency timeout blocks mission-critical transaction path
Shared App Gateway fault propagates across all backend workloads
RTO explodes as correlated failures cross unbounded blast radius
key_tradeoff: Stronger isolation via zones/stamps/bulkheads costs more complexity and redundancy spend

name: Disaster Preparedness
mantra: Drill recovery before disaster forces improvisation
when_to_apply: Designing BCDR for mission-critical workload tiers
Onboarding new regions or availability zones
After near-miss reveals untested recovery gaps
When compliance mandates documented RTO/RPO procedures
without_it: Untested ASR runbooks fail during regional outage, exceeding RTO
Ad-hoc panic responses extend downtime beyond SLA commitments
Geo-redundant backups corrupt silently, causing unrecoverable data loss
No defined disaster threshold triggers delayed escalation and role confusion
key_tradeoff: Regular drill investment costs operational overhead; skipping means unvalidated recovery assumptions

name: Standards
mantra: Define pattern once, execute consistently everywhere.
when_to_apply: Establishing repos, IaC templates, or pipeline definitions
Enforcing baseline config via Azure Policy assignments
Onboarding engineers to production operational processes
Troubleshooting incidents requiring predictable system state
without_it: Environment drift across regions breaks failover, extending RTO
Ad-hoc deployments bypass quality gates, causing production outages
Tribal knowledge bottlenecks incident response under pressure
Divergent Terraform/Bicep modules accumulate ungovernable technical debt
key_tradeoff: Rigid standards reduce deployment variance but slow adaptation to novel requirements.

name: Design For Business Requirements
mantra: Define SLOs before designing infrastructure
when_to_apply: Starting workload design or major redesign
Defining SLAs, SLOs, SLIs with stakeholders
Prioritizing reliability investments under budget constraints
When RTO/RPO targets drive active-active vs passive patterns
without_it: 99.999% design deployed for 99.9% workloads—wasted spend exponentially
Single-region deployment for revenue-critical path causes regional outage loss
Engineering promises SLA that architecture cannot physically deliver
Redundancy spend untraceable to specific business risk tolerance decisions
key_tradeoff: Each additional nine of availability doubles cost and operational complexity

name: RE:01 - Simplicity and Efficiency in Design
mantra: Kill every component you cannot justify.
when_to_apply: Designing new workload or major architecture redesign
Evaluating build-vs-buy or adding dependencies
When complexity creep inflates failure surface area
Choosing PaaS/SaaS versus self-managed IaaS components
without_it: Unjustified components multiply failure surfaces, degrading composite SLA
Hidden interdependencies extend MTTR beyond RTO targets
Restart sequencing across excess components inflates recovery time
Over-provisioned multi-region deployments burn budget without SLO justification
key_tradeoff: Fewer components improve reliability but may limit segmentation (SE:04) or redundancy (RE:05).

name: Shift Left
mantra: Catch defects early, fix cheaply, ship confidently
when_to_apply: Designing Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions pipelines
Production incidents trace to preventable code defects
Setting quality gates for Bicep/ARM deployments
Building health models into new workloads
without_it: Defects reach production; MTTR spikes, SLA breaches cascade
Security vulnerabilities deploy to AKS/App Service undetected
Slow feedback loops delay remediation by days or weeks
Reactive firefighting replaces proactive engineering culture
key_tradeoff: Early pipeline investment in testing/tooling costs velocity now, saves costly production failures later

name: Transparent Communication
mantra: Share status, context, decisions—nobody flies blind
when_to_apply: When cross-team DR war rooms coordinate failover
Deploying changes across shared Azure landing zones
Incident response requires real-time situational awareness
Onboarding engineers to operational runbooks and escalation paths
without_it: Duplicate deployments conflict across teams causing outages
DR escalations stall—RTO breached from missing stakeholder routing
Knowledge silos create human single points of failure
Blame culture emerges when incident context stays hidden
key_tradeoff: More shared signals means more noise—requires disciplined curation via dashboards and alerts

name: Monitor And Optimize Over Time
mantra: Right-size continuously—workloads drift, budgets follow.
when_to_apply: Post-deployment once real usage patterns emerge
Periodic cost-performance reviews via Log Analytics trends
Workload demand shifts from business or platform changes
Before/after major releases as pipeline quality gates
without_it: Over-provisioned VMs/databases drain budget undetected for months
Under-provisioned tiers cause latency spikes and SLA breaches
Stale baselines persist without Application Insights regression detection
No cost-to-value visibility—teams cannot justify or cut spend
key_tradeoff: Continuous optimization overhead (monitoring costs, team effort) versus silent resource drift inflating spend.

name: Shared Responsibility Principle
mantra: Own everything Microsoft does not manage
when_to_apply: Mapping IaaS/PaaS/SaaS responsibility boundaries during migration
Choosing zonal-pinned vs zone-redundant deployment models
Auditing compliance ownership gaps across shared boundaries
Triaging incidents—identify accountable party before escalating
without_it: Unpatched IaaS VM OS assumed Microsoft-managed triggers breach
Redundant failover code duplicates zone-redundant PaaS built-in capabilities
Compliance audit fails—no owner for zonal VMSS data replication
Incident MTTR spikes from provider-vs-customer accountability debates mid-outage
key_tradeoff: PaaS shrinks responsibility surface but surrenders granular infrastructure control

name: Risk Tolerance
mantra: Quantify acceptable failure before architecting anything
when_to_apply: Defining RTO/RPO/SLO targets per workload
Prioritizing resiliency investment across workload portfolio
Evaluating cost versus reliability tradeoffs
When onboarding new workloads to production
without_it: Zone-redundant deployments wasted on low-value internal tools
Critical workloads left single-region due to assumed safety
Stakeholder escalations during outages from misaligned SLOs
Inconsistent DR strategies: some workloads multi-region, peers unprotected
key_tradeoff: Higher risk tolerance cuts cost and complexity but increases business-impact exposure

name: Identity As A Security Perimeter
mantra: Authenticate every call, trust no network path
when_to_apply: Microservices communicating across public endpoints
Replacing VPN/firewall-only controls with zero-trust
When services lack VNet integration by design
Deploying multi-cloud or hybrid workloads
without_it: Lateral movement after network breach escalates to full compromise
Shared connection strings leak, granting ambient authority across services
No audit trail for service-to-service access patterns
Flat network compromise bypasses nonexistent perimeter controls
key_tradeoff: Per-call identity verification costs token lifecycle and Entra ID infrastructure complexity

name: Configuration As Code
mantra: Define every setting in version-controlled code
when_to_apply: Deploying workloads across multiple environments via CI/CD
Configuration drift causing production incidents
Compliance requires full change traceability and audit trails
Scaling infrastructure needing repeatable Bicep/Terraform provisioning
without_it: Environment drift causes silent failures; RTO extends during incident response
Manual portal changes lost; no rollback path after failed deployments
Audit gaps violate compliance; no proof of who changed what
Inconsistent deployments across stamps break multi-region reliability
key_tradeoff: Upfront DevOps engineering investment costs velocity now, buys consistency and auditability later

name: Security Design Principles
mantra: Bake Zero Trust into every architecture decision
when_to_apply: Starting workload architecture with STRIDE threat modeling
Reviewing designs for CIA triad gaps
Evaluating feature velocity against security posture tradeoffs
Preparing compliance audits or penetration testing cycles
without_it: Bolt-on security multiplies attack surface across WAF/DDoS/endpoint layers
Ad-hoc privilege grants violate least-privilege, enabling lateral movement
Unencrypted data at rest/transit causes compliance failures and breach exposure
Production vulnerability rework costs 10-100x versus design-phase mitigation
key_tradeoff: Stronger upfront security rigor costs initial design velocity and architectural flexibility

name: Azure Well-Architected Pillars
mantra: Balance five pillars or cascade failures across workloads
when_to_apply: Designing new workload across reliability/cost/security/performance/ops
When single-pillar optimization triggers cross-pillar regression
Conducting WAF assessment or architecture review
Resolving resource contention after deployment changes
without_it: Cost-optimized SKUs breach RTO/RPO targets during regional failover
NSG hardening adds latency breaking P99 performance baselines
Siloed teams over-optimize one pillar degrading Cosmos DB SLA tiers
Unbalanced trade-offs cause cascading resource exhaustion across regions
key_tradeoff: Strengthening one pillar (security, cost) directly taxes budget or degrades another pillar's SLA
